narrative.text:
The worktree is clean at the requested upstream base. I’ve read the design and checkpoint; W leaves admission resource limits explicitly unresolved, so I’m asking for that decision before encoding them.

The first real-transport channel tests are red: 0 pass / 25 fail; upstream accepts traffic the tests require it to refuse. The manager clarified three points: use the agreed bounded limits, reject stamp-bearing verdicts until slice D, and preserve pre-existing connector policy to honor O4. I’ll record those clarifications as deviations from the literal W/design wording.

The three lane commits are in place, and the expanded suite passes 115 tests. It covers real WebSocket ingress, stdio framework probes, late verdicts, overload, startup attestation, reconnects, and wake ceilings. Two additional red-before tests caught stale siblings reaching the hook and module requests bypassing an existing wake veto; both are fixed. Next are the no-hook baseline comparison and final gates.

The full Node 22.23.3 suite passed: **9,271 pass, 0 fail, 63 skipped**. The final ordering clarification also produced a useful red test: unknown-feature pushes with hints must get the existing feature error before the unsupported-hints refusal. I’ll make that small fix, then rerun the gates at the final commit.

The implementation is committed. Final typecheck and build passed on Node 22.23.3; the full test suite is still running. I’m preparing the report with the refusal matrix, red-before evidence, compatibility checks, and manager-approved deviations.

All 123 admission and compatibility tests pass, including the real-transport probes. The prior full suite also passed, but a final whitespace-only amend invalidated its commit-bound receipt, so I’m rerunning it at the exact final commit. No failures have appeared so far.

Final verification passed at `632f2e87`: typecheck, build, all 123 focused tests, and the full suite (9,276 passed, 63 skipped, zero failures). The worktree is clean. The report records all seven commits, the refusal matrix, evidence logs, approved deviations, and residual risks.
